characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Susato Mikotoba
characters.description1: A judicial assistant sent to Britain on a study tour. She's the epitome of a refined Japanese lady and a huge help to me always.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Herlock Sholmes
characters.description1: The world-famous 'great detective', above whose lodgings Miss Susato and I rent our own office and rooms.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Iris Wilson
characters.description1: An extraordinary young girl who lives with Mr Sholmes. She has a degree in medicine and is the author of a popular series of short stories.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Pop Windibank
characters.description1: The proprietor of a pawnbrokery on Baker Street that is regularly patronised by Mr Sholmes. He has a very great sense of responsibility to his clients.
characters.description2: The proprietor of a pawnbrokery on Baker Street that is regularly patronised by Mr Sholmes. He was shot dead by an unknown assailant.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Gina Lestrade
characters.description1: A young pickpocket who we first met during a trial two months ago. She and Iris have become firm friends since.
characters.description2: A young pickpocket who we first met during a trial two months ago. She's the defendant in this case, and was discovered at the scene of the crime alongside the victim.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Eggert Benedict → Ashley Graydon
characters.description1: A young English gentleman with an aloof and high-handed manner. He appeared at Windibank's pawnbrokery accusing Gina of stealing his redemption ticket.
characters.description2: A telegraph operator at the central communication system. He appeared at Windibank's pawnbrokery using the pseudonym Eggert Benedict.
characters.description3: A telegraph operator at the central communication system, whose last name was once Milverton years ago. He's a childhood friend of the Skulkin brothers.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Tobias Gregson
characters.description1: The detective inspector in charge of Scotland Yard's investigation of the case. He's stern and single-minded in his approach, and a great lover of fish and chips.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Mael Stronghart
characters.description1: The Lord Chief Justice, who wields absolute authority in judicial matters, including the appointment of lawyers. He's a thoroughly intimidating man.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Barok van Zieks
characters.description1: The infamous London-based prosecutor known as the Reaper of the Bailey. Further details about the man are not forthcoming.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Nash Skulkin
characters.description1: A witness to the event who broke into Windibank's on the night of the murder with his brother and accomplice Ringo. He claims to be a 'profeshnal baddie' by trade.

characters.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
characters.name: Ringo Skulkin
characters.description1: A witness to the event who broke into Windibank's on the night of the murder with his brother and accomplice Nash. He claims to be a 'profeshnal baddie' by trade.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Armband
evidences.description1: An armband I inherited from Kazuma. It identifies the wearer as a defence lawyer throughout the Empire of Japan.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Music Box Disk
evidences.description1: A metal disk used to play music in a mechanical music box. The piece of music, which remains unidentified, is stored on the disk by means of small protrusions.
evidences.description2: A metal disk used to play music in a mechanical music box. On the reverse side is a note that reads, 'For McGilded'.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: White Cat Photograph → Pawnbroker's Ticket (Box)
evidences.description1: A photograph depicting a sweet little white cat, obtained from Gina while interviewing her in her prison cell.
evidences.description2: A redemption ticket issued from the pawnbrokery owned by the victim, Mr Windibank, in the form of some hand-written notes on the back of a photograph. It was a ticket meant for the pawning of a small music box owned by Magnus McGilded

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Gina's Representation Papers
evidences.description1: The paperwork signed by Gina to put me in charge of her defence. Showing this to Scotland Yard detectives gains us access to the crime scene.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: White Cat Photograph #2 → Pawnbroker's Ticket (Coat)
evidences.description1: A photograph depicting a sweet little white cat. I feel as though I have another print just like this one...
evidences.description2: A redemption ticket issued from the pawnbrokery owned by the victim, Mr Windibank. There's what looks like a bloody fingermark on it.
evidences.description3: A redemption ticket issued from the pawnbrokery owned by the victim, Mr Windibank. The blood on it has been identified as Mr Mason's.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Blood Samples Portfolio
evidences.description1: A sample of blood analysed with a special chemical indicator developed by Mr Sholmes. Different people's blood turns different colours.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Iris's Story Manuscript
evidences.description1: A long, unpublished story that Mr Sholmes deposited at the pawnbrokery of the victim, Mr Windibank. It's entitled 'The Hound of the Baskervilles'.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: McGilded Case Notes
evidences.description1: Notes collated by Miss Susato about the McGilded case that we worked on two months ago.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Today's Paper
evidences.description1: This morning's paper, purchased by Iris. Gina's case features prominently.
evidences.description2: This morning's paper, which contains an article about government secrets being leaked to foreign agencies.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Autopsy Report
evidences.description1: A report prepared by the Scotland Yard coroner that confirms instant death due to a single bullet wound from the back. There are no other signs of trauma.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Crime Scene Photograph
evidences.description1: A photograph of the victim found murdered in the storeroom. It shows the single bullet wound in the man's back.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Crime Scene Floor Plan
evidences.description1: A plan of Windibank's pawnbrokery, the scene of the crime. It shows the relative positions of the main shop and the rear storeroom.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Windibank's Gun
evidences.description1: A gun belonging to the victim, Mr Windibank, that Gina was holding when she was found unconscious. There are signs of a single discharge.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Skulkin Brothers' Gun
evidences.description1: A firearm found in the possession of the Skulkin brothers upon their arrest. There are signs that a single round was fired.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Photograph of Gina
evidences.description1: A photograph taken automatically by the Red-Handed Recorder showing the scene a short time before the murder took place.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Post-Shooting Photograph
evidences.description1: A photograph taken automatically by the Red-Handed Recorder showing the scene after the murder had taken place.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Stereoscope
evidences.description1: A fold-up device that allows anybody to enjoy seeing things in three dimensions simply by looking through the eyepieces.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Sholmes's Pouch
evidences.description1: The pouch Mr Sholmes was wearing around his waist at the time of the shooting. One of the glass phials is smashed and there are scorch marks around it.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: The Third Bullet
evidences.description1: A projectile we discovered lodged in Mr Sholmes's pouch. It caused one of the phials to explode, injuring Mr Sholmes.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Small Music Box
evidences.description1: This strange music box only appears to be able to play a single tone. It was deposited at Windibank's two days before the black overcoat.

evidences.currentChapter: The Adventure of the Unspeakable Story
evidences.name: Cat-Flapomat
evidences.description1: A compact machine for the rapid creation of small flaps in larger doors, to allow cats to come and go freely.

testimonies.testimony: Alright, we did knock a few things over. But we weren't riflin' fer nuffin'!
It woz when we 'eard the gunshot, see. Made us both jump, an' all that stuff went flyin'.
Just before the gunshot, we 'eard a voice yellin' out, 'Gimme that gun!'
The bloke wot owned the place was 'oldin' a gun, so 'e should 'ave just fired instead of yellin' at the girl!

source.evidence_span: A photograph of the victim found murdered in the storeroom. It shows the single bullet wound in the man's back.
source.testimony_span: The bloke wot owned the place was 'oldin' a gun, so 'e should 'ave just fired instead of yellin' at the girl!
source.explanation: If the girl and the owner are waving gun at each other, they are most likely facing each other. But the victim was shot in the back according to the photograph.
source.context_span: Them two wavin' them guns at each other. Must've got pretty 'eated! I mean, just before 'e shouted out, we 'eard the geezer say, 'If ya don't wanna get shot...'!

testimonies.testimony: Lummy, it didn't 'alf gimme a fright! We woz thinkin' the shooter'd come out the door and get us next.
We stuck everyfin' back where we found it and scarpered...straight into 'im in the black.
We couldn't 'ave shot the pawnbroker, see! We never even 'ad a chance, did we?

turns.summarizedContext: The witness Nash is testifying about the events surrounding the gunshot incident.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims the girl and the owner were waving guns at each other.
Fact 2: The evidence suggests the owner was shot in the back.
Prop 1: If two person are waving guns at each other, they are likely facing each other.
Prop 2: If two person are facing each other, then it is unlikely that one can shot the back of the other.
